I can't produce this one as a WPL-AI document. The format I have supports workout programmes only, with no syntax for meals, macros, or food items. Any nutrition block I wrote would be invented syntax that the compiler would reject.

There's also a clinical reason to hand this off. For a client six months post-MI, nutrition should come from his cardiac rehab team or a registered dietitian:

- **Medication interactions:** He's likely on several cardiac drugs. Warfarin needs consistent vitamin K intake, some statins interact with grapefruit, and ACE inhibitors and ARBs can raise potassium, which affects salt substitutes and high-potassium foods.
- **Individual targets:** Sodium, fluid, and calorie targets depend on his ejection fraction, blood pressure, kidney function, and any diabetes. Only his care team has that data.
- **Scope of practice:** In most jurisdictions, therapeutic diets for a medical condition fall outside a personal trainer's remit.

Within scope, you can reinforce the general heart-healthy principles his rehab team will almost certainly endorse:

- A Mediterranean or DASH-style pattern: vegetables, fruit, whole grains, legumes, nuts, olive oil, and fish twice a week
- Limited processed meats, refined carbohydrates, sugary drinks, and ultra-processed foods
- Lower sodium, with the specific target set by his doctor
- Alcohol only within his physician's guidance
- Regular meals around sessions so he doesn't train fasted or straight after a heavy meal

If a nutrition plan type exists in WPL-AI, send me the grammar and I'll generate one that compiles, ideally built around targets from his dietitian.
